title: US Airways 1549: model the decision-maker’s time
focus: Validate scenarios against the time and information available to the operator, including recognition and decision delays.

sources.title: NTSB Aircraft Accident Report AAR-10/03
sources.locator: Section 1.16.3, Operational Factors and Human Performance Simulations, printed pp. 49–50; section 2.3.2; footnotes 88–89
sources.limitations: Relevant sections inspected; this is not a reconstruction of every event or finding.

facts.statement: The investigation examined the loss of thrust in both engines after a bird encounter and the subsequent Hudson River ditching.
Immediate-turn simulator attempts omitted recognition and decision time. The report describes one delayed return-to-LaGuardia attempt with a 35-second delay that did not succeed.

retrospective.boundary: Aircraft energy, available landing areas, crew cognition, procedures, air traffic control, cabin preparation, and rescue response form the emergency system.
interfaces: Failure cues → crew action: detection, interpretation, decision, and execution consume time.
Flight deck → cabin: protective preparation must fit the remaining time and information.

decision.question: What does a favorable simulator outcome establish about an actual emergency choice?
options: Treat the best trial as proof that a different choice was available.
Compare initial state, information, delays, training, and outcome variability before transferring a result.
decision.recommendation: Report scenario applicability before judging the historical decision.
decision.uncertainty: One delayed failed trial does not estimate a general success probability or prove all alternative paths impossible.

rows: Match position, energy, damage, and environment
Observed timing or justified sensitivity range
State which tested conditions support the conclusion

questions: Why is immediate response a strong modeling assumption?
What evidence would be needed to estimate success probability?
Explain the difference between a possible trajectory and an available decision.
answer_signals: Includes information and action latency in the system model.
Avoids extrapolating one run into a universal conclusion.
Communicates the limits of counterfactual evidence.
retrospective.transfer_exercise: Synthetic: an emergency controller proposes a recovery action that succeeds only with zero delay. Specify a fair comparison protocol.
retrospective.limits: Simulation results are attributed to the NTSB. This repository did not rerun the flight or conduct new pilot trials.
